title: Postmortem and Action Items: Continuous-batching stalls causing tail latency and fairness degradation
creator: Priya Nair
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 we observed a recurring capacity/regression event in the serving runtime where continuous batching entered long-lived batch-formation stalls. Symptoms were multi-minute tail latency spikes and pronounced fairness skew between tenant request classes. Impact: transient unavailability for latency-sensitive customers and multiple SLA alerts for 95/99th percentiles. Root causes: (1) BatchCoordinator slot allocation deadlock under skewed arrival patterns due to a small lock held across async callbacks; (2) scheduling window heuristics amplified by a moving-average request-size estimator that biased bundling toward large requests, starving small requests; (3) KV-cache cold starts at batch boundaries causing head-of-line blocking for some replicas. Immediate mitigation: rolled a configuration change (reduced max_batch_size and tightened scheduling window) and enabled emergency fallback routing to lightweight model-variant for affected customers. These mitigations restored acceptable p95 within 18 minutes but did not fully resolve fairness. This ticket tracks the postmortem findings and implements long-term fixes and tests.
comments: 2026-03-09 09:12 UTC - Detection: Pager triggered by p99 > 3s on /v1/generate. Automated alert pointed to batch-formation lag on a subset of GPU pools. Initial triage by on-call (Oliver Chen).

2026-03-09 09:40 UTC - Mitigation: Deployed runtime flag reduce_max_batch=0.6 and scheduling_window_ms=8 to force quicker flushes. Added emergency route to model-variant 'gpt-lite' for latency-critical customers. Incident commander: Priya Nair.

2026-03-09 11:05 UTC - Short-term RCA: Observed that BatchCoordinator was holding coordinator_lock across an async KV-cache prefetch callback. Under bursty input with mixed request sizes, the lock delayed slot handoffs and caused formation stalls. Also identified moving-average estimator skewing bundling decisions toward large requests.

2026-03-10 14:20 UTC - Action plan proposals reviewed in postmortem meeting. Decided on three parallel workstreams: (A) lock minimization and refactor of batch slot lifecycle, (B) fairness scheduler and per-tenant queue windows, (C) KV-cache prewarm + LRU warmup metrics. Owners assigned. Meeting notes: https://confluence.internal.redwood.ai/display/SERV/Postmortem+ENG-5723

2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - PR opened for coordinator_lock removal (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289. Early benchmarks show 45-70% reduction in median batch-formation latency in synthetic mixed-size workload. Note: still failing a tail-case where bursty small requests coincide with KV cold misses.

2026-03-12 16:30 UTC - Design doc for fairness scheduler: https://docs.redwood.ai/design/fair-batcher-v1. Comments from PM (Ava Martinez) requested a backwards-compatible flag and opt-in for Dedicated customers.

2026-03-13 10:15 UTC - Risk review: Proposed changes require careful rollout. Decided to gate by feature flag, run canary on 2 Dedicated pools, and enable traffic-shadowing for a week. Ops playbook updated: https://wiki.redwood.ai/playbooks/continuous-batching-incident

2026-03-14 08:45 UTC - QA plan: Create k6-based load harness with mixed request-size distributions and KV-hit-rates. Add chaos test for artificial KV cold starts. Assigned to: Jonas Becker. Estimated cycle: 2 weeks.

2026-03-14 12:00 UTC - PM acceptance criteria: p99 tail reduction to <2.0x baseline under 95th percentile traffic patterns and no more than 10% fairness delta between high and low priority tenants in synthetic tests (Ava Martinez).
action_items: AI-1 (owner: Oliver Chen) - Refactor BatchCoordinator to remove coordinator_lock from async hot path; introduce lock-free slot handoff. Deliverable: PR and microbench results. Due: 2026-03-25
AI-2 (owner: Jonas Becker) - Implement per-tenant fairness windows + bounded slot stealing policy. Provide design doc and e2e tests. Due: 2026-04-01
AI-3 (owner: Mira Patel) - KV-cache prewarm at batch boundaries with early warming signals; expose metrics for cold-miss ratio. Deliverable: runtime telemetry + config flag. Due: 2026-03-28
AI-4 (owner: Priya Nair) - Add load/chaos test scenarios (k6 + chaos) covering mixed-size bursts and KV cold starts. Integrate into CI and nightly perf runs. Due: 2026-03-22
AI-5 (owner: Ava Martinez) - Draft rollout plan and customer communication templates for Dedicated customers; include opt-in flag and rollback criteria. Due: 2026-03-20
AI-6 (owner: Engineering Infra) - Add dashboards and alert adjustments: split batch-formation-latency by tenant, pool, and request-size bucket. Update SLA runbook. Due: 2026-03-18
risks: Risk: Coordinator refactor could introduce subtle ordering regressions across KV-cache warmups. Mitigation: roll forward with canary and enable traffic-shadowing.
Risk: Fairness scheduler adds CPU overhead in hot paths. Mitigation: microbench and telemetry; feature-flag guard for Dedicated/Hosted tiers.
Risk: Aggressive prewarming increases memory pressure on replicas. Mitigation: limit concurrent prewarm count and monitor OOM indicators.
test_plan: Create synthetic traffic generator with configurable request-size mix (small/medium/large) and variable burstiness.
Simulate KV-cache cold-start patterns with controllable miss-rate and measure head-of-line impact.
Run e2e canary on two Dedicated pools with shadow traffic for 7 days before broader rollout.
Define SLO gates: p95 <= baseline*1.2 and fairness delta <= 10% for synthetic tenant mix.
